questions.question: Father of modern nursing is:
questions.explanation: Florence Nightingale (1820–1910) is universally recognized as the founder of modern nursing; established the Nightingale Training School (1860) and Environmental Theory.

explanations.A: Florence Nightingale (1820–1910) is universally recognized as the founder of modern nursing; established the Nightingale Training School (1860) and Environmental Theory.
explanations.B: Henderson — '14 basic needs' theorist.
explanations.C: Orem — Self-care deficit theorist.
explanations.D: Peplau — Interpersonal relations theorist (psychiatric nursing).

questions.question: Normal fetal heart rate range is:
questions.explanation: Normal baseline FHR is 110–160 bpm (NICHD/ACOG); <110 = bradycardia, >160 = tachycardia.

explanations.A: Lower bound suggests bradycardia.
explanations.B: Normal baseline FHR is 110–160 bpm (NICHD/ACOG); <110 = bradycardia, >160 = tachycardia.
explanations.C: Sustained tachycardia — abnormal.
explanations.D: Bradycardic range — concerning for hypoxia.

questions.question: BCG vaccine is given by which route?
questions.explanation: BCG is given intradermally (0.05 ml in newborn / 0.1 ml >1 mo) over the left deltoid to produce a wheal.

explanations.A: IM is used for DPT, Hep B, etc., not BCG.
explanations.B: SC is used for measles, MMR.
explanations.C: BCG is given intradermally (0.05 ml in newborn / 0.1 ml >1 mo) over the left deltoid to produce a wheal.
explanations.D: Oral route is for OPV and Rotavirus.

questions.question: The largest organ in the human body is:
questions.explanation: Skin is the largest organ of the body by surface area (~1.5–2 m²) and weight (~16% body weight).

explanations.A: Liver is the largest internal/solid organ but not the largest overall.
explanations.B: Skin is the largest organ of the body by surface area (~1.5–2 m²) and weight (~16% body weight).
explanations.C: Lungs are paired and lighter than skin.
explanations.D: Brain weighs ~1.4 kg — much smaller than skin.

questions.explanation: ORS was developed and promoted jointly by WHO and UNICEF, which is why both organisations appear on the standard formulation guidance.

questions.question: Which vitamin deficiency causes night blindness?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency impairs rhodopsin synthesis in rods → night blindness (nyctalopia), Bitot's spots, xerophthalmia.

explanations.A: Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency impairs rhodopsin synthesis in rods → night blindness (nyctalopia), Bitot's spots, xerophthalmia.
explanations.B: B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia and neuropathy.
explanations.C: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.
explanations.D: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets/osteomalacia.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cardinal sign of inflammation?
questions.explanation: The 4 cardinal signs are rubor, calor, dolor, tumor (swelling) — plus functio laesa (loss of function). Pallor is not on the list.

explanations.A: Rubor (redness) is a classic cardinal sign.
explanations.B: Calor (heat) is a classic cardinal sign.
explanations.C: Dolor (pain) is a classic cardinal sign.
explanations.D: The 4 cardinal signs are rubor, calor, dolor, tumor (swelling) — plus functio laesa (loss of function). Pallor is not on the list.

questions.question: The most common type of breech presentation is:
questions.explanation: Frank breech (hips flexed, knees extended, feet near head) accounts for ~50–70% of breech presentations.

explanations.A: Frank breech (hips flexed, knees extended, feet near head) accounts for ~50–70% of breech presentations.
explanations.B: Complete breech (hips and knees both flexed) is ~5–10%.
explanations.C: Footling (one or both feet presenting) is less common.
explanations.D: Kneeling breech is rare.

questions.question: Insulin should be stored at:
questions.explanation: Unopened insulin is stored at 2–8°C (refrigerator, not freezer). In-use pen/vial can be kept at room temperature (<25–30°C) for ~28 days.

explanations.A: Unopened insulin should be refrigerated; only the in-use vial may be at room temp up to ~28 days.
explanations.B: Unopened insulin is stored at 2–8°C (refrigerator, not freezer). In-use pen/vial can be kept at room temperature (<25–30°C) for ~28 days.
explanations.C: Freezing denatures insulin — never freeze.
explanations.D: Heat denatures the protein.

questions.question: Which is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The stapes (stirrup) of the middle ear is the smallest bone in the human body (~3 mm).

explanations.A: The stapes (stirrup) of the middle ear is the smallest bone in the human body (~3 mm).
explanations.B: Malleus is also a middle ear ossicle but larger than stapes.
explanations.C: Incus is the middle ear ossicle between malleus and stapes.
explanations.D: Lacrimal bone is small but larger than the stapes.

questions.question: The first vital sign to change with increasing intracranial pressure is:
questions.explanation: A change in level of consciousness (LOC) is the EARLIEST and most sensitive sign of increased ICP — must be detected before Cushing's triad appears.

explanations.A: BP changes (widened pulse pressure as part of Cushing's triad) are LATE signs.
explanations.B: Bradycardia is a late component of Cushing's triad.
explanations.C: Irregular respirations (Cheyne-Stokes) are late.
explanations.D: A change in level of consciousness (LOC) is the EARLIEST and most sensitive sign of increased ICP — must be detected before Cushing's triad appears.

questions.question: Which of the following is a positive symptom of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Hallucinations (along with delusions, disorganized speech/behavior) are positive symptoms (added behaviors).

explanations.A: Hallucinations (along with delusions, disorganized speech/behavior) are positive symptoms (added behaviors).
explanations.B: Flat affect is a negative symptom.
explanations.C: Avolition (lack of motivation) is a negative symptom.
explanations.D: Anhedonia (inability to experience pleasure) is a negative symptom.

questions.question: Tracheostomy tube is changed first time after:
questions.explanation: The first tracheostomy tube change is typically performed after 7 days (some references cite ≥72 h with surgical), allowing the tract to mature and reduce risk of accidental decannulation.

explanations.A: Too early — stoma tract not yet matured; risk of false passage.
explanations.B: Stoma still immature.
explanations.C: The first tracheostomy tube change is typically performed after 7 days (some references cite ≥72 h with surgical), allowing the tract to mature and reduce risk of accidental decannulation.
explanations.D: Too long — risk of biofilm and obstruction.

questions.question: The most common site of ectopic pregnancy is:
questions.explanation: ~95–97% of ectopic pregnancies occur in the fallopian tube; the ampulla is the single most common site (~70%).

explanations.A: Ovarian ectopic is rare (<1%).
explanations.B: Cervical ectopic is very rare.
explanations.C: ~95–97% of ectopic pregnancies occur in the fallopian tube; the ampulla is the single most common site (~70%).
explanations.D: Abdominal ectopic is rare (~1%).

questions.question: Which type of immunity is provided by breast milk to a newborn?
questions.explanation: Maternal IgA in breast milk and IgG transferred transplacentally provide passive natural immunity to the newborn.

explanations.B: Active artificial is via vaccination.
explanations.C: Maternal IgA in breast milk and IgG transferred transplacentally provide passive natural immunity to the newborn.

questions.question: The functional unit of the kidney is:
questions.explanation: The nephron (~1 million per kidney) is the structural and functional unit of the kidney; comprises glomerulus + renal tubule.

explanations.A: The nephron (~1 million per kidney) is the structural and functional unit of the kidney; comprises glomerulus + renal tubule.
explanations.B: Glomerulus is only the filtering component, part of the nephron.
explanations.C: Tubule is only part of the nephron.
